items.title: CommandLM: Data driven behavior level descriptor for ego vehicles
items.topic: CommandLM: Data driven behavior level descriptor for ego vehicles
items.summary: The arXiv paper introduces CommandLM, a multimodal large language model that generates human-readable behavior descriptions for ego vehicles from fused multi-sensor data, achieving CIDEr 0.67 and BERT-F1 0.88 scores. CommandLM processes temporally fused bird's-eye view representations from LiDAR and multi-camera inputs via a Q-Former adapter connected to a quantized, LoRA-fine-tuned large language model. This model is trained on the CommandLM-nuScenes dataset, producing intent-aware, interpretable captions suitable for planner supervision and safety auditing. The CommandLM model demonstrates strong linguistic and behavioral alignment, making it a valuable tool for autonomous driving applications.

items.title: MoRAL: Sensor-Grounded BEV Reasoning for Compact VLMs toward Edge-Oriented Autonomous Driving
items.topic: MoRAL: Sensor-Grounded BEV Reasoning for Compact VLMs toward Edge-Oriented Autonomous Driving
items.summary: The arXiv paper presents MoRAL, a two-stage fine-tuning pipeline that teaches the Cosmos-Reason2-2B model to read a physics-encoded Bird's Eye View (BEV) representation and reason over it for driving decisions. MoRAL's BEV image encodes LiDAR metric distance, object class, and radar Doppler velocity, allowing for reliable metric grounding and compact model size. The model is fine-tuned on 60,000 grounding records, achieving zero-shot baselines and demonstrating the potential for edge-oriented autonomous driving applications. MoRAL's approach enables the deployment of vision-language models on resource-constrained platforms, making it a significant contribution to the field of autonomous driving.

items.title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning for assisting Air Traffic Controllers
items.topic: Explainable Reinforcement Learning for assisting Air Traffic Controllers
items.summary: The arXiv paper proposes CARA, an intrinsically interpretable spatio-temporal framework for collision anticipation in autonomous driving. CARA derives domain-grounded risk concepts from accident narratives and aligns them with video frames via vision-language similarity, providing explicit risk evidence. The framework organizes risk concepts into evolving concept trajectories, enabling the anticipation of potential collisions. CARA's approach addresses the need for interpretable reasoning in autonomous driving, making it a valuable tool for improving safety and trust in autonomous vehicles. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of CARA in anticipating collisions and providing insights into the decision-making process.
